newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea crude quiet, but cash slips as pressure eases.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea crude quiet, but cash slips as pressure eases.

text.p: North Sea crude markets were quiet on Wednesday, but while wet differentials held firm, cash values drifted lower, as some of the previous day's heady buying pressure dissipated, traders said.

Physical crude sellers had a quiet morning, preferring to hold on to what little was left on their books for July in anticipation of still firmer numbers. "With so few cargoes around I think Brent trade is the only game left in town," said one trader. Two cargoes were due to be nominated from the paper chains today, both loading July 17-19.
But outright values drifted lower, with IPE August Brent 25 cents off at $18.55 a barrel in reaction to disappointing U.S. industry stock data.

Dealers said that as well as the two July 12-14 Brent cargoes confirmed sold on Tuesday at undisclosed prices, two more may have been passed from a French major to a trading house at a price related to this week's dated numbers.
The deals, for the loading dates of July 13-15 and 14-16, were not immediately confirmed by the counter-parties.
Wet Brent, although not heard actively offered on Wednesday morning, was talked at -0.05/0.00 against August Brent.
A Forties cargo loading July 24-26 was heard to have been traded twice at dated Brent +40 cents on Tuesday, underlining the steadiness of differentials.
But some of the strength experienced late yesterday was ebbing out of the cash market, with dealers saying some calm replacing the near-panic generated by the short-term physical tightness.
The July/August spread drifted down five cents to +0.05/0.15, while Aug/Sept and Sept/Oct lost several cents to talk at -0.07/-0.05 and -0.09/-0.06.
